rules.statement: Implement single-use (replay) checks as one atomic add-if-absent operation, never as a read followed by a write.
rules.why: If you read and then write, two concurrent presentations of the same proof or assertion can both be accepted. That breaks the promise of atomic recording.
rules.check: Look for replay or nonce checks that call Get/Contains and then Set on a store such as IDistributedCache, instead of a single atomic TryAdd or SET NX operation.

rules.statement: Do not use IDistributedCache for single-use or replay state, because it has no atomic add-if-absent operation.
rules.why: IDistributedCache only offers get and set, so it cannot express an atomic single-use check.
rules.check: Look for replay caches, nonce stores or single-use records built on IDistributedCache.

rules.statement: A library must not register host-wide infrastructure services such as IDistributedCache. The host's composition root chooses them.
rules.why: When a library registers a shared host service, it makes that choice for the host and for every other consumer of the service.
rules.check: Look for library DI extension methods that call AddDistributedMemoryCache or register other host-wide infrastructure services.

rules.statement: State that must hold across replicas must not rely on per-process defaults without a swappable shared adapter. Any request may reach any replica.
rules.why: With a per-replica default, a nonce issued by one replica was rejected by another, and a replay sent to a different replica was accepted.
rules.check: Look for nonce, replay or freshness state kept in process memory with no adapter port that a multi-replica deployment can replace.

rules.statement: Build keys for a shared store as a purpose prefix, the tenant, and a digest (for example base64url SHA-256) of the length-prefixed UTF-8 components. Do not join request-supplied values with a delimiter.
rules.why: Joining with a delimiter is ambiguous ("a:b","c" collides with "a","b:c") and has no length limit. Without the tenant in the key, one tenant's records collide with another's.
rules.check: Look for store keys built by string concatenation or interpolation of request-supplied values with ':' or another separator, unhashed values of unbounded length, or keys with no tenant.

rules.statement: Single-use and freshness checks must fail closed: if the store is unreachable or the requested expiry is not in the future, reject the request.
rules.why: Accepting a request the server cannot check would let replays through.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks around shared-state calls that treat an error as success, or that record or accept keys whose expiry is already in the past.

rules.statement: When the server computes a time-to-live for a shared store, compute it from the local clock (preferably the injected TimeProvider) and round it up to whole units. Do not depend on the store server's clock.
rules.why: Expiry should not depend on the server's clock. Rounding up keeps the key from expiring early.
rules.check: Look for TTL calculations that round down or truncate, or that use absolute expiry timestamps interpreted by the remote server.

rules.statement: Startup validation errors about connection strings must never echo the connection string.
rules.why: A connection string may contain a password.
rules.check: Look for exception messages or log calls that include the raw connection string value.

rules.statement: Put optional backend adapters that bring heavy client dependencies (such as a Redis client) in separate opt-in packages, not in the core or turnkey package.
rules.why: Otherwise every consumer, including single-replica self-hosters, would carry the dependency.
rules.check: Look for backend client package references (for example StackExchange.Redis) added to a core or turnkey server project.

rules.statement: An adapter that connects to an external store should not abort host startup when the store is unreachable. It should reconnect in the background and expose a readiness-tagged health check.
rules.why: This keeps startup resilient while still reporting outages through readiness.
rules.check: Look for store connections that use AbortOnConnectFail=true or block startup, and for a missing health check tagged 'ready'.
